max_range_fft_size.COMMENTS: maximum range FFT size for all radar projects

max_doppler_fft_size.COMMENTS: maximum Doppler FFT size for all radar projects

max_range_bins.COMMENTS: maximum range bins for all radar projects

platform_id.COMMENTS: Radar name should be defined in Core.Platforms

verify_cal_type.COMMENTS: SMC sections should not have a duplicated Cal_Type

reset_time_max.COMMENTS: Chirp reset time shall be < 8 us in TI's MMIC to prevent the MMIC from going into power saving mode, which will introduce large transient signal in ADC

reset_time_min.COMMENTS: Chirp reset time shall be > 2 us in TI's MMIC.

settling_time_min.COMMENTS: Chirp settling time shall be > 2 us in TI's MMIC.

k_selective_rest_ratio_threshold.COMMENTS: Threshold to decide whether or not to run REST

k_sum_rx_chan_factor.COMMENTS: Factor to adjust max value over Rx NCI to get proper scaling

k_fast_estimation_sample.COMMENTS: Number of samples to use for DC estimation / IDM threshold calculation

k_ddma_doppler_bin_shift.COMMENTS: Offset (in Doppler bins) between the carriers

k_rest_threshold_factor.COMMENTS: REST Threshold for HWA use in masking signal

SHA.COMMENTS: SHA of the whole workbook, calculate during release

advchirpcfg_chirp_param_idx.COMMENTS: 0 - CHIRP_PROFILE_SELECT, 1 - CHIRP_FREQ_START_VAR, 2 - CHIRP_FREQ_SLOPE_VAR, 3 - CHIRP_IDLE_TIME_VAR, 4 - CHIRP_ADC_START_TIME_VAR, 5 - CHIRP_TX_EN, 6 - CHIRP_BPM_VAL, 7 - TX0_PHASE_SHIFTER, 8 - TX1_PHASE_SHIFTER, 9 - TX2_PHASE_SHIFTER

advchirpcfg_reset_mode.COMMENTS: 0 - Reset at end of Frame, 1 - Reset at end of subframe, 2 - Reset at end of burst, 3-255   Reserved

advchirpcfg_delta_reset_period.COMMENTS: 0 - Reset only as per RESET MODE option, 1 - Delta increment is disabled, 2-32768 - Reset every M chirps in addition to RESET MODE option

advchirpcfg_delta_param_update_period.COMMENTS: 0 - Delta increment is disabled, 1-N - The fixed delta value will be incremented once after every N chirps.

advchirpcfg_lut_reset_period.COMMENTS: 0 - Reset only as per RESET MODE option, 1 - Fixed 0th indexed LUT value programmed for all chirps, 2-32768 - Reset every M chirps in addition to RESET MODE option

advchirpcfg_lut_param_update_period.COMMENTS: 0 - Fixed 0th indexed LUT value programmed for all chirps, 1-K - Index to LUT will be incremented once after every K chirps and corresponding LUT value is used, Range : 0-16384

advchirpcfg_lut_burst_index_offset.COMMENTS: 0 - The LUT start index is 0 for first chirp of all the bursts, 1-P - LUT index start offset for each burst

advchirpcfg_lut_sf_index_offset.COMMENTS: 0 - The LUT start index is 0 for first chirp in a burst of all SF , 1-P - LUT index start offset for each sub-frame (SF)

advchirpcfg_lut_chirp_param_size.COMMENTS: CHIRP_FREQ_START_VAR: 0 - 4 bytes, 1 - 2 bytes, 2 - 1 byte, CHIRP_IDLE_TIME_VAR: 0 - 2 bytes, 1 - 1 byte, CHIRP_ADC_START_TIME_VAR: 0 - 2 bytes,1 - 1 byte

advchirpcfg_lut_chirp_param_scale.COMMENTS: Range : 0-16, The actual parameter value for the defined chirp is given by: 2^ LUT_CHIRP_PARAM_SCALE * LUT_PARAM_VALUE

advchirpcfg_max_tx_ph_shift_int_dither.COMMENTS: This field is applicable only if SFn_CHIRP_PARAM_DELTA increment is enabled for Phase shifter dithers. It controls the TX phase quantization. Range : 0-1023

advframeseqcfg_num_sub_frames.COMMENTS: Number of sub frames enabled in this frame Valid range: 1 to 4

advframeseqcfg_force_profile.COMMENTS: 0x0 The profile index set in rlSetChirpConfig API governs which profile is used when that chirp is transmitted                                        0x1 The profile index indicated in rlSetChirpConfig API is ignored and all the chirps in each sub frame use a single profile as indicated by that sub frame's profile forceProfileIdx.

advframeseqcfg_loop_back_cfg.COMMENTS: b0 - LOOPBACK_CFG_EN 0 - Disable 1 - Enable, b2:1 - SUB_FRAME_ID for which the loopback configuration applies,b7:3 - RESERVED

advframeseqcfg_sub_frame_trigger.COMMENTS: 0 - Disabled, default mode, i.e no trigger is required in SW triggered mode and a pulse trigger is required every burst start            1 - Enabled, Need to trigger each sub-frame either by SW in software triggered mode or HW SYNC_IN line in hardware triggered mode

advframeseqcfg_force_profile_idx.COMMENTS: This is applicable only if FORCE_SINGLE_PROFILE is set to 1

advframeseqcfg_chirp_start_idx.COMMENTS: Start Index of Chirp Valid range = 0-511

advframeseqcfg_num_chirps.COMMENTS: Num of unique Chirps per burst including start index Valid range = 1 - 512. 0 for LUT

advframeseqcfg_num_loops.COMMENTS: No. of times to loop through the unique chirps in each burst, without gaps, using HW. Valid range = 1 to 255

advframeseqcfg_burst_periodicity.COMMENTS:
burstPeriodicity >= (numLoops)* (sum total of all unique chirp times per burst) + InterBurstBlankTime.  1 LSB = 5 ns   
								Valid range: 100 uS to 1.342 sec   Same as framePeriodicty in rlFrameCfg

advframeseqcfg_chirp_start_idx_offset.COMMENTS:
Chirp Start address increment for next burst, next_burst_chirp_start_idx = last_chirp_end_index + h_ChirpStartIdxIncr 0 - 511, 
								0 = 2nd burst = 1st burst

advframeseqcfg_num_burst.COMMENTS: Num of bursts in the sub-frame. Valid Range: 1 - 512

advframeseqcfg_num_burst_loops.COMMENTS: Number of times to loop over the set of above defined bursts, in the sub frame. Valid Range: 1 - 64

advframeseqcfg_sub_frame_periodicity.COMMENTS:
subFramePeriodicity >= Sum total time of all bursts + InterSubFrameBlankTime, Where, 
								Sum total time of all bursts = numOfBurstLoops * numOfBurst * burstPeriodicity. 1 LSB = 5 ns. Valid range 100 us to 1.342 s

advframeseqcfg_num_frames.COMMENTS:
Number of frames to transmit (1 frame = all enabled sub frames). 
								If set to 0, frames are transmitted endlessly till Frame Stop message is received. Valid range: 0 to 65535

advframeseqcfg_trigger_select.COMMENTS: 0x0001 SWTRIGGER (Software API based triggering) 0x0002 HWTRIGGER (Hardware SYNC_IN based triggering)

advframeseqcfg_frame_trig_delay.COMMENTS:
Optional time delay from sync_in trigger to the occurance of frame chirps. 
								Applicable only in SINGLECHIP sensor applications. 1 lsb = 5 ns. Typical range is 0 to few tens of micro seconds

chancfg_cascading.COMMENTS:
0x0000 SINGLECHIP: Single mmWave sensor application, 
								0x0001 MULTICHIP_MASTER: Multiple mmwave sensor application. This mmwave is  the master chip and generates LO and conveys to other mmwave sensor,
								0x0002 MULTICHIP_SLAVE: Multiple mmwave sensor application. This mmwave is a slave chip and uses LO conveyed to it by the master mmwave sensor

chancfg_tx_channel_en.COMMENTS:
b0 TX0 Channel Enable, 0 - Disable TX Channel 0, 1 - Enable TX Channel ,
								b1 TX1 Channel Enable, 0 - Disable TX Channel 1, 
								1 - Enable TX Channel 1, b2 TX2 Channel Enable, 0 - Disable TX Channel 2, 1 - Enable TX Channel 2, b15:3 - RESERVED

chancfg_rx_channel_en.COMMENTS:
0x1111, RX Channel Bitmap, b0 RX0 Channel Enable,  0 - Disable RX Channel 0,  1 - Enable RX Channel 0, 
								b1 RX1 Channel Enable,  0 - Disable RX Channel 1,  1 - Enable RX Channel 1, b2 RX2 Channel Enable,  0 - Disable RX Channel 2,  
								1 - Enable RX Channel 2, b3 RX3 Channel Enable,  0 - Disable RX Channel 3,  1 - Enable RX Channel 3, b15:4 - RESERVED

testsource_test_obj0.COMMENTS:

k_reg_dcest_shift.COMMENTS: Programmable right shift for DC estimation: Right bit-shift applied to all 12 DC accumulator outputs. Cannot be bypassed. Accumulator outputs are scaled by 2^(8 + 6 + DCEST_SHIFT). Valid range for this register is 0 to 14 (i.e., scaling of 2^14 to 2^28). Note that DCEST_SHIFT = 15 is not supported

k_reg_dcest_scale.COMMENTS: Programmable fine scaling for DC estimation: 9-bit scale applied to all 12 DC accumulators. This is followed by right shift and truncation. Multiplies the accumulator output by DCEST_SCALE/256. Default value is 256 giving a scale of 1.0. Setting it to 128, gives a scale of 0.5

k_reg_intf_stats_magdiff_shift.COMMENTS: Programmable right shift for Interference statistics MagDiff: Right bit-shift applied to the interference magdiff accumulator. Total right shift of the accumulator is 2^(3+6+INTF_STATS_MAGDIFF_SHIFT). Valid range for this register is 0 to 6 (i.e., the right shift can’t be more than 2^15).

k_reg_intf_stats_magdiff_scale.COMMENTS: Programmable fine scaling for Interference statistics MagDiff: Scaling applied to INTF_STATS_MAGDIFFACC<n> from interference statistics block.

The parameters of the window are assumed to be monotonically ascending. For example : val = floor(hanning(14)*32) INTF_MITG_WINDOW_PARAM = val(2:6); If a shorter window (of length less than 5) is desired, some of the earlier window parameters can be set to 31. This sets the window parameter to 31/32 (or ~1).

k_reg_dcest_reset_mode.COMMENTS: 2-bit field that controls the reset behavior for all 12 DC accumulators 00 : Hold Accumulator state without updating 01 : Reserved 10 : Reset at start of param-set (i.e., per-chirp DC estimation). 11 : Reset at start of param-set only if loop counter is 0 (i.e., per frame DC estimation)

k_reg_intf_loc_thresh_en.COMMENTS: Enable/Disable for Interference localization (marking out): This register bit controls the enable/disable for the interference marking (setting Interference Indicator Bit) feature. The feature is enabled if this register bit is set to 1.

k_reg_intf_loc_thresh_mode.COMMENTS: Interference detection mode selection: This register is used to control the mode for interference detection in the Interference localization block. 00 : Magnitude OR Magnitude difference 01: Only Magnitude difference 10: Only Magnitude 11 : Magnitude AND Magnitude difference

k_reg_loc_thresh_sel.COMMENTS: Select the source of interference threshold 0 : User-defined threshold via INTERFTHRESH_MAG_SW and INTERFTHRESH_MAGDIFF_SW 1 : Single threshold based on built-in interference statistics outputs using sum value across collected interference statistics 2 : Threshold based on built-in interference statistics outputs, with each statistic being used for corresponding iteration (RX channel)

k_reg_int_stats_reset_mode.COMMENTS: Reset mode control for Interference statistics accumulators: Controls the reset behavior for all 12 magnitude and magdiff accumulators. 00 : Hold Accumulator state without updating 01 : Free-running accumulator mode 10 : Reset at start of parameter-set (i.e.,per-chirp accumulation). 11 : Reset at start of parameter-set only if loop counter is 0 (i.e., per-frame)

k_reg_dcsub_en.COMMENTS: Enable or Disable DC subtraction. If this register bit is set to 1, DC subtraction is enabled. Else, it is disabled.

k_reg_dcsub_sel.COMMENTS: Source select for DC subtraction: 0 : Value comes from processor via DC_SW_I<n> & DC_SW_Q<n> 1: Value comes from built-in DC estimation hardware, i.e., DCEST_I<n> & DCEST_Q<n>

k_reg_intf_mitg_en.COMMENTS: If this bit is set, the interference mitigation path is activated, else it is bypassed.

k_reg_intf_mitg_path_sel.COMMENTS: Based on the value of this register, one of the three paths is activated. 00b: Simple Zeroing out 01b: Windowed Zeroing out 10b: Linear Interpolation 11b: Reserved

k_reg_intf_mitg_cntthresh.COMMENTS: The (total) number of non-zero IIB within the ‘Hysteresis window’ should exceed this threshold for the sample-under-test to be considered to be affected by interference. Range : 0 to 31.

k_reg_intf_mitg_right_hyst_ord.COMMENTS: The length of the IIB array considered on the right side of (i.e. after) the sample under test. Range : 0 to 15.

k_reg_intf_mitg_left_hyst_ord.COMMENTS: The length of the IIB array considered on the right side of (i.e. after) the sample under test. Range : 0 to 15.

k_reg_cmp_dither_enable.COMMENTS: The register enables dithering. Dithering prevents periodic quantization patterns from resulting in spurs. The dither source provides 3 bits of dither for every sample. Note : This register has to be set to 1 for proper operation of the hardware

k_rest_reg_cfar_thr_scale.COMMENTS: Threshold scale factor: This register is used to specify the threshold scale factor. This value is used to either multiply or add to the ‘surrounding noise level’ to determine the threshold used for detection of the present cell under test. If logarithmic CFAR mode is disabled (in magnitude or magnitude-squared mode), then the register value is multiplied with the surrounding noise level to determine the threshold, else it is added to the surrounding noise level. In the former case, this 18-bit register is interpreted as a 14.4 value. In the latter case (logarithmic mode), the 18-bit register is interpreted as a 7.11 value.

k_rest_reg_cmp_dither_enable.COMMENTS: The register enables dithering. Dithering prevents periodic quantization patterns from resulting in spurs. The dither source provides 3 bits of dither for every sample. Note : This register has to be set to 1 for proper operation of the hardware

k_rest_cfar_ca_mode.COMMENTS: CFAR noise averaging mode: This register configures the noise averaging mode in the CFAR detector from one of these options – CFAR-CA, CFAR-CAGO, CFAR-CASO, CFAR-OS. 00b – CFAR-CA 01b – CFAR-CAGO 10b – CFAR-CASO 11b – CFAR-OS

k_rest_cfar_log_mode.COMMENTS: CFAR linear or logarithmic mode: This register is one of the registers used to specify whether the CFAR detector operates in linear or logarithmic mode. If this register bit is set, then the CFAR detector operates in logarithmic mode, which means that the threshold scale factor is added to (instead of multiplied with) the surrounding noise level value to determine the threshold. Note that this mode is meaningful only when the input samples to the CFAR detector are log- magnitude samples (see CFAR_INP_MODE as well). If this register bit is 0, then the logarithmic mode is disabled, in which case, the threshold scale factor is multiplied with (instead of added to) the surrounding noise level to determine the threshold. This mode is meaningful when magnitude or magnitude squared samples are fed to the CFAR detector.

k_rest_cfar_abs_mode.COMMENTS: CFAR magnitude, mag-squared or log-mag mode: This register is used to specify which of the three computations, namely Magnitude, Mag- squared or Log-Magnitude, is enabled inside the CFAR engine prior to CFAR detection. This register is only relevant when CFAR_INP_MODE is 0 (complex samples are fed to CFAR engine). 00b – Magnitude-squared 01b – Not valid 10b – Magnitude (using JPL approximation) 11b – Log2-Magnitude (using LUT approximation)

k_rest_car_avg_right.COMMENTS: Number of right-side samples for noise level computation: This register is very similar to the above, except that this register specifies the averaging to the right of the cell under test. In most cases, it is expected that CFAR_AVG_RIGHT has the same value as CFAR_AVG_LEFT. In non-cyclic modes of CFAR, CFAR_AVG_RIGHT must be programmed equal to CFAR_AVG_LEFT.

k_rest_car_avg_left.COMMENTS: Number of right-side samples for noise level computation: This register is very similar to the above, except that this register specifies the averaging to the right of the cell under test. In most cases, it is expected that CFAR_AVG_RIGHT has the same value as CFAR_AVG_LEFT. In non-cyclic modes of CFAR, CFAR_AVG_RIGHT must be programmed equal to CFAR_AVG_LEFT.

k_rest_reg_cfar_noisediv.COMMENTS: CFAR noise average division factor: This parameter is applicable only in CFAR-CA modes and it is not applicable in CFAR OS mode. This register specifies the division factor with which the noise sum calculated from the left and right noise windows are divided, in order to get the final surrounding noise average value. The division factor is equal to 2^ CFAR_NOISE_DIV. Therefore, only powers-of-2 division are possible, even though the number of samples specified in CFAR_AVG_LEFT and CFAR_AVG_RIGHT are not restricted to powers of 2. The surrounding noise average value obtained after the division is multiplied or added with CFAR_THRESH to determine the final threshold used to compare the cell under test for detection. The maximum allowed value for this register is 8, which gives a division factor of 256.

k_rest_cfar_guard_int.COMMENTS: Number of guard cells: This register specifies the number of guard cells to ignore on either side of the cell under test. If this register value is 3, then three guard cells on the left side and three guard cells on the right side are ignored. Only the noise samples beyond this guard region are used for calculating the surrounding noise level.

k_rest_cfar_os_kval.COMMENTS: K-th value for ordered statistic: This register is useful only in CFAR-OS mode, where it indicates the parameter K. From the sorted list of left and right noise samples, the K’th lowest value is used as the noise sample. This is a zero-based count – for instance, if this register value is 27, then the 28th lowest element in the sorted array is selected. Note that since CFAR-OS supports a maximum of 64 samples each on left and right side, the maximum size of the vector to sort is 128, and hence the maximum valid value of CFAR_OS_KVALUE register is 127.

This value is used to either multiply or add to the ‘surrounding noise level’ to determine the threshold used for detection of the present cell under test. If logarithmic CFAR mode is disabled (in magnitude or magnitude-squared mode), then the register value is multiplied with the surrounding noise level to determine the threshold, else it is added to the surrounding noise level.
